data.content:
1	---
2	name: horizon-start
3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
4	---
5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.
71	
72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
74	orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
75	stand before proposing work.
76	
77	One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
78	for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
79	`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
80	check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
81	resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
82	the run's original plan.)
83	
84	## Then, before you start
85	
86	- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
87	  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
88	- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
89	  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
90	  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
91	- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
92	  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
94	  `horizon-inbox`.
95	
96	Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
97	smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
98	here.
99

1	Everything committed and verified. Nine commits; the review landed and I acted on all three of its findings.
2	
3	## Summary
4	
5	Closed **two of the three remaining clauses** in Wave 5's T4 block — then discovered, and corrected, that my own claim about what remained was wrong. Nine commits, all sorry-free, root build green at **9164 jobs, exit 0**, axiom probe clean on all four keystones with a control that still reports `sorryAx`.
6	
7	The honest headline is two-part: the mathematics advanced further than the worksheet predicted, and my accounting of the *residue* was too optimistic twice. Both corrections are in the documents that made the claims.
8	
9	## Progress
10	
11	- `Tangent/TwoChartNormalize.lean` (new, 267L, 0 sorries): **(iii-c1)** — every Čech Picard class representable on the two-chart cover is in the comparison's range.
12	- `Tangent/TwoChartRepresentable.lean` (new, 327L, 0 sorries): **(iii-c2-Zar)** — a class trivial on each chart *is* a two-chart class. No `IsAffine`, no dual numbers, no curve, not even selector surjectivity.
13	- `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md`: +§§6.8–6.11, written before every Lean edit as T4 binds; includes three retractions and a start-of-session checklist with the import graph measured acyclic.
14	- `informal/w5-s-worksheet.md` §2.1: retracted my own "S1 needs an upstream mathlib PR" — `private` hides the name, not the proof.
15	- Coordination: both threads; flagged a red root build in another lane's file (owner fixed it, since verified green) and a stale-index hazard (two AJC lanes disarmed it); three memories.
16	
17	The transferable finding: the transport cost both projects had priced — rewrite a cochain's *type*, then `subst` four `Bool` cases — is **zero** if you restrict along an *inequality* instead, because `≤` of opens is a `Prop`. A predicted [M] became [S], and the four-case split vanished from the main lemma.
18	
19	## Issues
20	
21	- **I claimed "(iii-c2-aff) alone stands between AJCR and the numeral" twice. Not measured, and wrong.** Two further steps are absent at HEAD: a **carrier translation** (T2 computes Čech H¹ of `DualNumber`-of-*original* sections; the comparison consumes *thickened* sections, and nothing composes the bridge) and the **reduction square** intertwining the two halves. Both bookkeeping, neither landed. I found the square myself via another lane's safeguard; the carrier gap I would not have caught — the reviewer did.
22	- **Three phantom names in my own docstrings** (`..._surjective_of_mk`, `twoChartClass_surjOn_of_chartTrivial`). Fixed. This is precisely the trap one of my own memories records, and I walked into it while writing the file that cites the lesson.
23	- Verification note: per a same-day finding that `lean_minimal_hypotheses` can give a false all-clear, I confirmed `hL` load-bearing by **deleting it** and observing failure, not by the tool.
24	- The janitor never reported (third such background-helper death on this task); filed to human. The work-reviewer *did* report, as an inbox item.
25	
26	## Why I stopped
27	
28	**Partly advanced, not complete.** The residue is now correctly stated as three statements: (iii-c2-aff) — the last clause needing geometry — plus the carrier translation and the reduction square. I did not start (iii-c2-aff) because the remaining budget favoured leaving a measured, corrected hand-off over a half-built module. S1 remains a hypothesis by design; **P1 untouched and still DD-gated**, as instructed.
29	
30	## Next
31	
32	Take the two bookkeeping steps first — they are cheap, they are now precisely specified in §6.10, and landing them makes (iii-c2-aff) genuinely the last thing. Then (iii-c2-aff) per §6.11, whose step 1 is already struck out (`relCover` supplies the affine thickened cover). Watch the sheaf→module step at clause (i): the sibling project was flagged for eliding exactly that.
33

673	A scoped read of the tree (subagent, read-only) established one negative and one positive fact
674	that together change the shape of (iii-c2).
675	
676	**The negative, and it is the honest crux.** *Nothing in the tree — at any generality — says
677	"a `CechPic` class trivial on every member of a cover is `CechPic.mk` of a class on that
678	cover".* Six search phrasings, plus a direct audit of `EffectivityMoving.lean`,
679	`EffectivityTrivialization.lean` and `CechPicSurjective.lean`. In particular
680	`EffectivityMoving.lean` is *one-directional*: `Opens.cechPicClass … = 1 ⟹ CechPic.map O.ι L = 1`
681	and nothing back. §6.6 called that file "the landed bridge that makes (iii-c2) assembly rather
682	than construction" — **that reading was too generous**, and I am retracting it here rather than
683	letting a later session discover it. `EffectivityMoving` bridges *into* the chart-triviality
684	hypothesis; the step *from* chart triviality to representability is unbuilt.
685	
686	**The positive: chart triviality is exactly the right hypothesis, and it is Zariski.** Write
687	the target as
688	
689	> **(iii-c2-Zar)** `L : X.CechPic` with `CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1` for both `s : Bool`
690	> ⟹ `L` is representable on `twoChartCover V sel hmem`.
691	
692	*No `IsAffine`, no `k[ε]`, no curve.* The proof:
693	
694	1. `L = mk 𝒩 γ.class` (`CechPic.ind`).
695	2. For each `s`, feed `CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1` to the **landed**
696	   `exists_trimmed_trivializing_of_cechPicMap_ι_eq_one` (`EffectivityTrivialization.lean:75`,
697	   *no affineness hypothesis*): a family `t s b : Γ(X, 𝒩.opens b ⊓ V s)ˣ` with
698	   `t s b · γ(b,b') = t s b'` on trimmed overlaps.
699	3. **The overlap unit.** The family `b ↦ t false b · (t true b)⁻¹`, on the opens
700	   `𝒩.opens b ⊓ V false ⊓ V true`, is **independent of `b`**: from step 2 at both `s`,
701	   `t s b' = t s b · γ(b,b')`, so the ratio picks up `γ(b,b')⁻¹ · … · γ(b,b')` — which cancels
702	   because *sections of a scheme are commutative rings and their units commute*. The opens
703	   cover `V false ⊓ V true`, so the landed `exists_unitsRestrict_eq`
704	   (`RefinementInjectivity.lean:76`) glues them to `u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ`.
705	4. **The comparison.** On the common refinement `𝒲 := 𝒩 ⊓ twoChartCover`, whose member at `b`
706	   is `𝒩.opens b ⊓ V (sel b)` (`PointedCover.inf_opens`), the `0`-cochain
707	   `β b := t (sel b) b` conjugates `γ` into `twoChartCocycle u`:
708	   `β b · γ(b,b') = t (sel b) b' `, and `twoChartPairUnit u (sel b) (sel b') · β b'` is the same
709	   by the glue property of `u` at the point `b'`. Then `mk_unitsRes` on both sides.
710	
711	**Two typing notes, both the §6.8 lesson again.** (a) `t` is indexed by `s : Bool`, so
712	`t (sel b) b : Γ(X, 𝒩.opens b ⊓ V (sel b))ˣ` typechecks **on the nose** at the `𝒲`-member — the
713	`Bool` index is instantiated, never transported. (b) The four-case split in step 4 is again an
714	*identification* of `twoChartPairUnit` values, not a transport: diagonals are `t s b' · (t s b')⁻¹`,
715	the mixed pair is the glue property, the reversed pair its inverse.
716	
717	**What this buys, and it is the real point.** (iii-c2) is now

1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
36	
37	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
38	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
39	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
40	
41	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
42	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
43	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
44	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
45	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
46	the shared index drifts behind.
47	
48	Consequences, all three binding:
49	
50	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
51	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
52	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
53	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
54	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
55	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
56	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
57	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
58	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
59	
60	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
61	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
62	
63	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
64	
65	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
66	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
67	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
68	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
69	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
70	
71	```bash
72	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
73	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
74	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
75	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
76	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
77	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
78	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
79	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
80	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
81	    fi
82	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
83	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
84	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
85	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
86	    fi
87	  fi
88	  sleep 10
89	done
90	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
91	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
92	```
93	
94	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
95	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
96	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
97	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
98	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
99	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
100	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
101	
102	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
103	
104	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
105	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
106	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
107	retry-looping.
108	
109	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
110	
111	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
112	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
113	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
114	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
115	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
116	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
117	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
118	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
119	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
120	
121	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
122	
123	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
124	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
125	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
126	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
127	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
128	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
129	
130	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
131	
132	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
133	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
134	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
135	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
136	> usually accompanies it.
137	
138	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
139	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
140	warning.
141	
142	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
143	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
144	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
145	their work and turns one incident into two.
146	
147	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
148	
149	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
150	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
151	workspaces must use their own lock paths.
152	
153	### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
154	
155	The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
156	projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
157	over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
158	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
159	OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.
160	
161	The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
162	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
163	(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
164	at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
165	
166	### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
167	
168	§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
169	`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
170	not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
171	also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
172	provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
173	
174	Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
175	
176	* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
177	  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
178	* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
179	  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
180	  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
181	  check you substituted.

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RefinementInjectivity
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineCech
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TruncExpCech
9	
10	/-!
11	# The two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units embeds in the Picard group (W5-T4 clause (iii-a)/(iii-b))
12	
13	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the two-chart Čech cohomology of units
14	
15	```
16	Ȟ¹(V₀,V₁ ; 𝒪ˣ)  =  Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)
17	```
18	
19	maps to the definitional Picard group `X.CechPic`, **injectively**
20	(`Scheme.twoChartClass_injective`). This file builds that map and proves the injectivity.
21	
22	## Why this file exists: clauses (iii-a) and (iii-b), which are not about dual numbers
23	
24	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6 splits the Wave-5 residue "clause (iii)" — the last input to
25	the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 dimension identity — into three parts, and observes that **two of
26	them contain no dual numbers, no curves and no `H¹`**. Those two are exactly this file:
27	
28	* **(iii-a)** the comparison homomorphism `twoChartClass` exists;
29	* **(iii-b)** it is injective.
30	
31	Both are general statements about a scheme with a two-open cover, so they are stated here at
32	that generality rather than at `C ×_k Spec k[ε]`. The remaining part, **(iii-c)**
33	(surjectivity onto the `ε`-kernel), is the only one that needs the thickening; it consumes
34	`DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` and lives elsewhere.
35	
36	The two-chart Čech quotient here is the **same carrier** the truncated-exponential engine of
37	`Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes: `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the two restriction
38	maps. So `twoChartClass` is precisely the arrow that connects the (landed) T2 engine to the
39	(definitional) Picard group, in the direction the tangent computation needs.
40	
41	## Implementation notes
42	
43	`CechPic` is built on **pointed** covers — one open per point — so a two-open cover enters
44	through a selector `sel : X → Bool` with `x ∈ V (sel x)`, exactly as
45	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieceIndex` and `thetaFieldChartIndex` do elsewhere in the tree.
46	Indexing the charts by `Bool` (rather than by two named opens) is what makes the cocycle law a
47	`cases`-bash that closes uniformly.
48	
49	The cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u` has pair values `1` on the diagonal, `u` at
50	`(0,1)` and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)` (`Scheme.twoChartPairUnit`).
51	
52	**A negative result, recorded so it is not retried** (worksheet §6.2): the slick spelling
53	`pairUnit s t = u ^ (δ t − δ s)`, which would close the cocycle law by `zpow_add` alone, does
54	**not** typecheck. On the diagonal the ambient open `T` need only be `≤ V s`, where `u` — a
55	section on `V₀ ⊓ V₁` — cannot be restricted at all. The exponent trick needs a unit on the
56	union and there is none. The eight-case `cases` bash is the honest route, and it is three
57	lines.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartPairUnit` — the pair values, with
62	  `twoChartPairUnit_trans` (the cocycle law, all eight `Bool` cases) and
63	  `twoChartPairUnit_mul` (multiplicativity in the overlap unit).
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCover` — the pointed cover of a selector.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCocycle` — the unit Čech 1-cocycle of an overlap unit.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClassHom` — `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ →* X.CechPic`, the map before
67	  passing to the quotient, with `twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff` (the kernel computation, where
68	  refinement injectivity enters).
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClass` — **(iii-a)**: the induced homomorphism
70	  `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits → X.CechPic`.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClass_injective` — **(iii-b)**.
72	
73	## What the surjectivity hypothesis is for
74	
75	`twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff` and everything downstream take `hsel : Function.Surjective sel`
76	— the selector must actually use both charts. This is not bookkeeping: the cobounding
77	`0`-cochain produced by refinement injectivity is indexed by *points*, and turning it into a
78	pair of *chart* units needs one point assigned to each chart. See that lemma's docstring.
79	
80	A second trap recorded at `twoChartCoboundary_of_pairRelation`: transporting a chart unit
81	along `sel i = false` with `▸` produces an ill-typed motive, because the type of a section
82	depends on the open which depends on the `Bool`. Abstracting the chart indices as variables
83	and using `subst` avoids the transport entirely.
84	
85	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, proof of Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020).
86	-/
87	
88	set_option autoImplicit false
89	
90	universe u
91	
92	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
93	
94	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
95	
96	namespace Scheme
97	
98	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : Bool → X.Opens}
99	
100	/-- `Units.map` of the section-restriction ring map **is** `unitsRestrict`, definitionally.
101	Named so that the two spellings — the one `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` is stated in and
102	the one the Čech cocycle API uses — can be rewritten into each other. -/
103	@[simp]
104	theorem unitsMap_resHom {U W : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) :
105	    Units.map (X.resHom h).toMonoidHom = X.unitsRestrict h :=
106	  rfl
107	
108	/-! ## The pair values of an overlap unit -/
109	
110	/-- **The pair values of the two-chart cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u`.** Trivial on
111	the diagonal, `u` at `(0,1)`, and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)`.
112	
113	The diagonal entries are forced to be `1`: a cocycle value at `(s,s)` lives on opens contained
114	in `V s` alone, where an overlap section has no meaning. This is also why the `zpow` spelling
115	of these values does not typecheck — see the module docstring. -/
116	noncomputable def twoChartPairUnit (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
117	    ∀ s t : Bool, Γ(X, V s ⊓ V t)ˣ
118	  | false, false => 1
119	  | true,  true  => 1
120	  | false, true  => u

255	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) := by
256	  refine (Over.isPushout_sections X (overSpec k A)
257	    (isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A) hV hV').of_iso
258	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)) (Iso.refl _) (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)) (Iso.refl _)
259	    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
260	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
261	    rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
262	  · have h : (overSpec k A).hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (overSpec k A).hom).ge =
263	        (overSpec k A).hom.appTop :=
264	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
265	    rw [h, overSpec_hom]
266	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
267	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
268	  · rw [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
269	    exact (Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc _ _).symm
270	
271	/-- **Base change of sections, comparison isomorphism** (in `CommRingCat`):
272	`Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≅ Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)` for a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`.
273	On pure tensors this is the product of the two pullbacks; see
274	`Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul`. -/
275	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso {V : X.left.Opens}
276	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
277	    CommRingCat.of (Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) ≅
278	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
279	  (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).isoIsPushout _ _
280	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')
281	
282	/-- **Base change of sections** (brick 1 of the separatedness ledger, design §4.4): for `X`
283	over the field `k`, a commutative `k`-algebra `A` and a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`, the ring
284	equivalence `Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)`, sending `s ⊗ a` to
285	the product of the pullbacks of `s` (along the first projection) and of `a` (along the
286	second). The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` is `Over.sectionsAlgebra`. -/
287	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChange {V : X.left.Opens}
288	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
289	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
290	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
291	  (Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso X A hV hV').commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
292	
293	/-- `Over.sectionsBaseChange` for an affine open `V` (affine opens are qcqs) — the form
294	pinned by design §4.4 brick 1. -/
295	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen {V : X.left.Opens}
296	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
297	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
298	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
299	  Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV.isCompact hV.isQuasiSeparated
300	
301	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one {V : X.left.Opens}
302	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
303	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) :
304	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ 1) =
305	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s :=
306	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inl_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
307	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom s)
308	
309	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
310	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) (a : A) :
311	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (1 ⊗ₜ a) =
312	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
313	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
314	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a :=
315	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inr_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
316	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom a)
317	
318	/-- The base-change equivalence on a pure tensor: `s ⊗ a` goes to the product of the
319	pullback of `s` along the first projection and the pullback of `a` along the second. -/
320	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
321	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
322	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) (a : A) :
323	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ a) =
324	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s *
325	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
326	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
327	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a := by
328	  have h : (s ⊗ₜ[k] a : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) = (s ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ a) := by
329	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul]
330	  rw [h, map_mul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one, Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul]
331	
332	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
333	/-- **Naturality of the base-change equivalence in the open**: for `W ≤ V` (both qcqs),
334	restricting the base-changed section is base-changing the restriction. The map on tensor
335	products is `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` of the restriction `Over.resAlgHom` and the
336	identity of `A`. -/
337	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_naturality {V W : X.left.Opens}
338	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
339	    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set X.left))
340	    (hWV : W ≤ V) (x : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) :
341	    (X ⊗ overSpec k A).left.presheaf.map
342	        (homOfLE (show (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤
343	          (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V by gcongr)).op
344	      (Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' x) =
345	      Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hW hW'
346	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Over.resAlgHom X hWV) (AlgHom.id k A) x) := by
347	  induction x with
348	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
349	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
350	  | tmul s a =>
351	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, Over.resAlgHom_apply,
352	      Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, map_mul]
353	    congr 1
354	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
355	        Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
356	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Category.assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
357	
358	end TensorFace

9	/-!
10	# The tangent space of the Jacobian at the identity (W5-T5, the scalar-identity spine)
11	
12	The Wave-5 tangent statements phrased against the pinned representability datum
13	`(d : JacobianData C)` (roadmap `AJCR.w5-av.t5`), assembling the generic kit of
14	`Tangent/` into the two forms Wave 5 actually consumes:
15	
16	```
17	Dual κ(e) (m_e/m_e²)  ≃  T_e(d.J)  ≃  ker (Pic⁰(Spec k[ε]) →* Pic⁰(Spec k))
18	```
19	
20	and, under the **one** remaining numerical input, the frozen scalar identity
21	`dim_κ(e) m_e/m_e² = genus C` together with its additive consequence
22	`m_e/m_e² ≃+ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`.
23	
24	## The scalar-identity-first discipline (w5-worksheet D6), and what it buys
25	
26	The W12 lesson recorded in the worksheet is that dimension transport must go
27	through **one** `finrank` identity, followed by **one** non-canonical `≃+` — not
28	through a chain of additive equivalences each carrying its own linearity
29	bookkeeping. This file is that discipline made structural:
30	
31	* `JacobianData.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` is the representability leg,
32	  unconditional and sorry-free. It is a bijection of **sets**; it deliberately
33	  does *not* claim to transport dimension (a bare `Equiv` cannot).
34	* `JacobianData.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus` isolates the numerical
35	  content as a **hypothesis** `hdim`. That hypothesis is what the T3/T4 chain must
36	  deliver.
37	* `JacobianData.nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1` then produces the additive
38	  equivalence from the count, once.
39	
40	So the Wave-5 tangent keystone is, at HEAD, reduced to a statement about the
41	`ε`-kernel of `pic0Functor` — **but note precisely which statement**. The
42	`ε`-kernel *bijection* above is not enough on its own: it is a bijection of sets,
43	and `finrank` does not transport along one. What `hdim` needs is the **semilinear
44	comparison** — an additive equivalence plus the intertwining law across
45	`κ(e) ≃+* k` — fed through `finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` (proved
46	below, unconditionally). Stating T3/T4's target as a bare kernel bijection would
47	leave the count unreachable; this is the same residue the AJC sibling isolated as
48	`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`. See inbox I-0513.
49	
50	Note that the
51	identity point of `d.J` needs no rationality hypothesis: it is the image of the
52	group-object unit, hence a section, hence automatically `k`-rational
53	(`bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section`).
54	
55	## Main declarations
56	
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.identitySection` — the `k`-rational identity
58	  point of `d.J`, with `identitySection_isSection`.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.tangentSpaceCotangentDual` — `T_0(d.J)` is the
60	  `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space at the identity.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` — `T_0(d.J)` is
62	  the `ε`-kernel of `pic0Functor C` (the representability leg, applied).
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_pic0Kernel` — the two
64	  composed: the cotangent dual at the identity *is* the `ε`-kernel.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace` — the
66	  cotangent space at the identity is finite-dimensional (from
67	  `d.locallyOfFiniteType`).
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` —
69	  **unconditional**: `finrank` transports across a scalar *bijection* given an
70	  additive equivalence and the intertwining law. The bridge that makes the count
71	  reachable at all.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus` /
73	  `nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1` — the frozen scalar identity and its
74	  additive consequence, each conditional on the T3/T4 semilinear comparison.
75	
76	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020);
77	Milne, "Abelian varieties", Prop. 2.1.
78	-/
79	
80	set_option autoImplicit false
81	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
82	
83	universe u v
84	
85	open CategoryTheory IsLocalRing Opposite
86	
87	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
88	
89	namespace JacobianData
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
93	
94	/-- **The identity point of the Jacobian.** The underlying scheme morphism
95	`Spec k ⟶ d.J.left` of the group-object unit — the `k`-rational point at which
96	Wave 5 computes the tangent space. -/
97	noncomputable def identitySection (d : JacobianData C) : Spec (.of k) ⟶ d.J.left :=
98	  letI := d.grpObj
99	  GroupScheme.identitySection d.J
100	
101	/-- The identity point is a section of the structural morphism (the unit is a
102	morphism of `Over (Spec k)` out of the monoidal unit). -/
103	lemma identitySection_isSection (d : JacobianData C) :
104	    d.identitySection ≫ d.J.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) :=
105	  letI := d.grpObj
106	  GroupScheme.identitySection_comp d.J
107	
108	/-- **The tangent space of the Jacobian at the identity, as a cotangent dual**
109	(Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11, LHS). The pointed dual-number points of `d.J` at the
110	identity form the `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space `m_e/m_e²`. No
111	rationality hypothesis is needed: the identity point is a section, hence
112	automatically `k`-rational. -/
113	noncomputable def tangentSpaceCotangentDual (d : JacobianData C) :
114	    pointedDualNumberPoints d.J d.identitySection ≃
115	      Module.Dual
116	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
117	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))) :=
118	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
119	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
120	  overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual d.J (d.identitySection_isSection)
121	    (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim _ _))
122	
123	/-- **The representability leg, applied** (Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11): the tangent
124	space of `d.J` at the identity is the **kernel** of the restriction
125	homomorphism
126	
127	```
128	Pic⁰_{C/k}(Spec k[ε]) →* Pic⁰_{C/k}(Spec k)
129	```
130	
131	along the `ε ↦ 0` point. Immediate from `pointedDualNumberPointsEquivKer` at the
132	pinned datum `d.rep`, whose functor is `pic0Functor C` composed with the
133	forgetful functors — note the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` typing of `rep` is exactly what
134	makes the group-valued kernel meaningful, and `JacobianData` owns that massage.
135	
136	⚠ A bijection of **sets**: it does not transport `finrank`. That is the point of
137	the scalar-identity-first discipline — see the module docstring. -/
138	noncomputable def tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel (d : JacobianData C) :
139	    pointedDualNumberPoints d.J d.identitySection ≃
140	      {a : (pic0Functor C).obj (op (overDualNumber k)) //
141	        ((pic0Functor C).map (overDualNumberZero k).op).hom a = 1} :=
142	  pointedDualNumberPointsEquivKer d.J (pic0Functor C) d.rep d.identitySection_isSection
143	
144	/-- **The two legs composed**: the `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space at
145	the identity of `d.J` *is* the `ε`-kernel of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`. This is the statement
146	the T3/T4 chain computes against, and the one whose dimension T5 counts. -/
147	noncomputable def cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_pic0Kernel (d : JacobianData C) :
148	    Module.Dual
149	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
150	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
151	      ≃ {a : (pic0Functor C).obj (op (overDualNumber k)) //
152	          ((pic0Functor C).map (overDualNumberZero k).op).hom a = 1} :=
153	  d.tangentSpaceCotangentDual.symm.trans d.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel
154	
155	/-- **Finite-dimensionality of the cotangent space at the identity.** The
156	Jacobian is locally of finite type over `k` by the datum's certificate, hence
157	locally Noetherian, so `m_e/m_e²` is a finite-dimensional `κ(e)`-vector space —
158	the input any dimension count needs. -/
159	theorem finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace (d : JacobianData C) :
160	    FiniteDimensional
161	      (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
162	      (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))) :=
163	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
164	  letI : IsLocallyNoetherian d.J.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian d.J.hom
165	  inferInstance
166	
167	/-! ## The frozen scalar identity, and the bridge T3/T4 must actually cross
168	
169	Everything above is unconditional. What follows carries the numerical input as an
170	explicit hypothesis, named once:
171	
172	```
173	hdim : Module.finrank κ(e) (m_e/m_e²) = genus C
174	```
175	
176	Keeping it a hypothesis rather than a `sorry` is the w5-worksheet §0(4) rule
177	(never register a staged fact).
178	
179	**What `hdim` needs, stated precisely — the `ε`-kernel bijection alone is NOT
180	enough.** `tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` is a bijection of *sets* (it says so on
181	its own docstring) and a bare `Equiv` does not determine `finrank`. So T3/T4's
182	kernel computation does not by itself give `hdim`: additionally required is an
183	**additive** equivalence together with the intertwining law across the
184	residue-field bijection `κ(e) → k`, because the two sides are modules over
185	genuinely different rings — neither `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq` nor a
186	`restrictScalars` argument applies.
187	
188	`finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` below is exactly that bridge, and it
189	is unconditional. With it in hand the residual obligation on T3/T4 is the
190	**semilinear comparison**: a scalar bijection `i`, an additive equivalence `j`
191	from `Dual κ(e) (m_e/m_e²)` to `H¹(C,𝒪)`, and `j (r • x) = i r • j x`. That is
192	the honest target to state T3/T4 against — and it is the same residue the AJC
193	sibling isolated (`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`), which is why
194	porting the generic kit without this bridge would have left the count
195	unreachable. Found by fresh-context review; see inbox I-0513. -/
196	
197	/-- **`finrank` across a scalar bijection** (the linearity bridge the Wave-5
198	count needs, and the reason the `ε`-kernel *set* bijection is insufficient on its
199	own). If `i : R → R'` is a bijection of scalars, `j : M ≃+ M₁` an additive
200	equivalence, and the two intertwine (`j (r • m) = i r • j m`), then `M` and `M₁`
201	have equal `finrank` over their respective rings.
202	
203	`i` need only be a **bijection**, not a ring homomorphism, and the module
204	structures live over genuinely different rings — which is precisely the situation
205	of the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 count, comparing a `κ(e)`-dimension with a
206	`k`-dimension across `κ(e) ≃+* k`. Mathlib has this at the level of
207	`Module.rank` (`rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv`) but not in `finrank` form; this is the
208	`Module.finrank = toNat ∘ Module.rank` unfolding of it. -/
209	theorem finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul
210	    {R : Type*} {R' : Type*} {M M₁ : Type v} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
211	    [Semiring R'] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [Module R' M₁]
212	    (i : R → R') (j : M ≃+ M₁) (hi : Function.Bijective i)
213	    (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) :
214	    Module.finrank R M = Module.finrank R' M₁ := by
215	  unfold Module.finrank
216	  rw [rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv i j hi hc]
217	
218	variable (d : JacobianData C)
219	
220	/-- **The frozen scalar identity** `dim_κ(e) T₀(d.J) = genus C`, conditional on
221	the T3/T4 count. Stated in cotangent form: since `T₀(d.J)` is by
222	`tangentSpaceCotangentDual` the `κ(e)`-linear dual of `m_e/m_e²` and the latter
223	is finite-dimensional (`finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace`), the dual has the same
224	dimension, so this single `finrank` equation *is* the Wave-5 dimension
225	statement — no further transport is needed or wanted (w5-worksheet D6).
226	
227	The hypothesis is exactly what T3/T4 produce; nothing else in Wave 5 needs the
228	`ε`-kernel in any other form. -/
229	theorem finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus
230	    (hdim : Module.finrank
231	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
232	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
233	      = genus C) :
234	    Module.finrank
235	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
236	        (Module.Dual
237	          (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
238	          (CotangentSpace
239	            (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))))
240	      = genus C := by
241	  rw [Subspace.dual_finrank_eq]
242	  exact hdim
243	
244	/-- **The Wave-5 tangent keystone, additively** (Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11): the
245	cotangent space at the identity of `d.J` is additively isomorphic to
246	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, given the scalar identity. This is the "one non-canonical `≃+`
247	after one `finrank` identity" of the D6 discipline: the equivalence is produced
248	*once*, by choosing bases on both sides and transporting along `κ(e) ≃+* k`
249	(`nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq`), and it is `Nonempty` because
250	that choice is not canonical.
251	
252	`genus C` is by definition `finrank k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Challenge.lean`), so the
253	hypothesis really is the dimension comparison of the two sides. -/
254	theorem nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1
255	    [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
256	    (hdim : Module.finrank
257	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
258	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
259	      = genus C) :
260	    Nonempty
261	      (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))
262	        ≃+ Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
263	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
264	  nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq d.J d.identitySection_isSection
265	    (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) hdim
266	
267	end JacobianData

260	  | false => v₁⁻¹
261	  | true  => v₂

263	/-- **The coboundary relation for `twoChartCob`**: if `u = ρ₀(v₁) · ρ₁(v₂)` then the

265	cases; the two off-diagonal ones are where the hypothesis is spent. -/
266	theorem twoChartCob_spec (v₁ : Γ(X, V false)ˣ) (v₂ : Γ(X, V true)ˣ)
267	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ)
268	    (hv : Units.map (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)).toMonoidHom v₁
269	        * Units.map (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)).toMonoidHom v₂ = u)

272	      = X.unitsRestrict hb (twoChartCob v₁ v₂ t) := by
273	  subst hv
274	  cases s <;> cases t <;>

10	/-!
11	# Chart triviality over the dual numbers
12	
13	The **first input of the tangent/`H¹` geometric middle** of
14	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`), in the
15	concrete dual-number spelling: *an invertible module over `A[ε]` whose restriction along
16	`ε ↦ 0` is trivial is itself trivial.*
17	
18	Geometrically this is the statement that an invertible sheaf on `C ×_k Spec k[ε]` trivial
19	along `ε ↦ 0` is trivial on each base-changed affine chart of a 2-affine cover — which is
20	what turns the class into a single transition unit on the overlap and so feeds the two-chart
21	Čech unit-cocycle engine of `Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6. On an affine chart
22	`V = Spec A` the base change is `Spec A[ε]` (`DualNumber.baseChangeAlgEquiv` of that file,
23	combined with mathlib's `pullbackSpecIso`), so the geometric statement reduces to the
24	algebra proved here.
25	
26	## Main results
27	
28	* `DualNumber.augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot` — the augmentation ideal `ker(A[ε] → A)` is
29	  **square-zero**. This is where "first-order deformation" enters, and it is the only
30	  property of the dual numbers the argument uses.
31	* `DualNumber.ker_fstHom_eq_span_eps` — that kernel is exactly `(ε)`, so a consumer holding
32	  either spelling can use the other.
33	* `DualNumber.isNilpotent_ker_fstHom` / `DualNumber.isNilpotent_span_eps` — nilpotency, the
34	  hypothesis of the general statement in `Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean`.
35	* `DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` — the chart statement: an invertible `A[ε]`-module in
36	  which every element agrees with a multiple of a fixed `m` modulo `(ε)·M` is free.
37	
38	## What this does and does not close
39	
40	It closes the *chart-triviality* clause of the geometric middle, for arbitrary affine charts
41	and with no finiteness hypothesis on the sections (see the discussion in
42	`Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean` — the nilpotent Nakayama iteration is what buys that).
43	The two remaining clauses of the middle are the identification
44	`Γ(V ×_k Spec k[ε], 𝒪) ≅ Γ(V, 𝒪)[ε]` — already available as
45	`DualNumber.baseChangeAlgEquiv` — and the statement that under these identifications a
46	kernel element goes to its transition unit, which is the genuinely cocycle-level step and
47	is still open.
48	
49	As recorded in the docstring of `semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok` and
50	confirmed from the sibling project (inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28), none of this needs Hilbert 90
51	or any henselian cover-splitting brick: the thickening is square-zero, which is precisely
52	the hypothesis discharged by `augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot` here.

68	and the `snd` component of a product is `a.fst * b.snd + b.fst * a.snd`.

70	This is the single property of the dual numbers that the chart-triviality argument uses —
71	everything else is the general nilpotent statement of
72	`Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean`. -/

76	  have ha' : a.fst = 0 := ha

78	  refine Ideal.mem_bot.mpr (TrivSqZeroExt.ext ?_ ?_)
79	  · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.fst_mul, ha']
80	  · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.snd_mul, ha', hb']

83	representability side produces the kernel of the restriction along `ε ↦ 0`, the cocycle side
84	produces the ideal generated by `ε` — so the identification is recorded once here.

86	Left to right: an element `x` with `x.fst = 0` is `ε · inl x.snd`. Right to left: `ε` has
87	vanishing constant term. -/

89	    RingHom.ker (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom A A A) = Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)} := by
90	  refine le_antisymm (fun x hx => ?_) (Ideal.span_le.mpr ?_)
91	  · have hx' : x.fst = 0 := hx
92	    refine Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mpr ⟨TrivSqZeroExt.inl x.snd, ?_⟩
93	    refine TrivSqZeroExt.ext ?_ ?_
94	    · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.fst_mul, hx']
95	    · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.snd_mul]

97	    rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy

99	    change (ε : DualNumber A).fst = 0

102	/-- The augmentation ideal is nilpotent, being square-zero. -/
103	theorem isNilpotent_ker_fstHom : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom A A A)) :=
104	  Ideal.isNilpotent_of_mul_self_eq_bot (augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot A)

107	theorem isNilpotent_span_eps : IsNilpotent (Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)}) := by

113	restriction along `ε ↦ 0` is generated by the image of `m`, hence trivial — is free.

132	theorem free_of_cyclic_mod_eps
133	    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (DualNumber A) M]
134	    [Module.Invertible (DualNumber A) M] (m : M)
135	    (h : ∀ x : M, ∃ r : DualNumber A,

9	/-!
10	# Affine two-chart covers, and their pullback along the base-change projection
11	
12	An **affine two-chart cover** of a scheme `Y` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover`) is a pair of affine
13	opens `V₀, V₁` covering `Y` whose overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is again affine. This file provides:
14	
15	* the structure `Scheme.AffineTwoCover`;
16	* **existence** for the challenge curve: the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve
17	  `C/k` admits an affine two-chart cover (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`), obtained
18	  as the preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` under a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹`
19	  (`exists_isFinite_toP1`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1`); the overlap is affine because it
20	  is the preimage of the affine chart overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`;
21	* **stability under base change**: an affine two-chart cover of `C.left` pulls back, along the
22	  first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`, to an affine two-chart cover of
23	  `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, for any `k`-algebra `R` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`).
24	  The key input is that the first projection is an affine morphism: it is the base change of
25	  `overSpec k R ⟶ Spec k` (itself affine, being a morphism between affine schemes) along
26	  `C.hom` (`Over.isAffineHom_fst_left`), and preimages of affine opens under an affine
27	  morphism are affine.
28	
29	## Main declarations
30	
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover` — the structure.
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve` — existence for the curve.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isAffineHom_fst_left` — the first projection of a base change along
34	  an affine morphism is affine.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd` — the pullback of an affine two-chart
36	  cover along the first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`.
37	-/

49	/-- An **affine two-chart cover** of a scheme `Y`: two affine opens `V₀, V₁` covering `Y`
50	whose overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is again affine. -/
51	structure Scheme.AffineTwoCover (Y : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
52	  /-- The first chart. -/
53	  V₀ : Y.Opens
54	  /-- The second chart. -/
55	  V₁ : Y.Opens
56	  /-- The first chart is affine. -/
57	  isAffineOpen₀ : IsAffineOpen V₀

59	  isAffineOpen₁ : IsAffineOpen V₁
60	  /-- The two charts cover `Y`. -/
61	  sup_eq_top : V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤
62	  /-- The overlap of the two charts is affine. -/
63	  isAffineOpen_inf : IsAffineOpen (V₀ ⊓ V₁)

112	/-- **The first projection of a base change along an affine morphism is affine**: for `X, T`
113	objects of `Over S`, `(fst X T).left` is (up to the defeq `Over.fst_left`/`Over.tensorObj_left`)
114	the pullback of `T.hom` along `X.hom`, i.e. `Limits.pullback.fst X.hom T.hom`
115	(`Over.isPullback_left`, flipped so that the affine leg `T.hom` lines up with the class field
116	`IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback`); affineness is stable under base change
117	(`isAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange`). -/
118	instance Over.isAffineHom_fst_left {S : Scheme.{u}} (X T : Over S) [IsAffineHom T.hom] :
119	    IsAffineHom (fst X T).left :=
120	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsAffineHom) (Over.isPullback_left X T).flip ‹_›

123	identifies it with `Spec (.of A)`, so that instance search finds it without unfolding the
124	`abbrev overSpec`). -/
125	instance isAffine_overSpec_left {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
126	    [Algebra k A] : IsAffine (overSpec k A).left := by
127	  rw [overSpec_left]; infer_instance
128	
129	/-- The structure morphism `overSpec k A ⟶ Spec k` is affine: it is a morphism between affine
130	schemes. -/
131	instance isAffineHom_overSpec_hom {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
132	    [Algebra k A] : IsAffineHom (overSpec k A).hom :=
133	  isAffineHom_of_isAffine _

139	/-- **Base change of an affine two-chart cover**: an affine two-chart cover `D` of `C.left`
140	pulls back, along the first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`, to an affine
141	two-chart cover of `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, for any `k`-algebra `R`. The charts are the
142	preimages of `D`'s charts under the first projection. All four fields follow from `D`'s
143	fields: the first projection is an affine morphism (`Over.isAffineHom_fst_left`, since
144	`overSpec k R ⟶ Spec k` is a morphism between affine schemes hence affine), preimage of an
145	affine open under an affine morphism is affine, and preimage commutes with `⊔`, `⊓`, `⊤`. -/
146	noncomputable def Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd (D : C.left.AffineTwoCover)
147	    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
148	    (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left.AffineTwoCover where
149	  V₀ := (fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀
150	  V₁ := (fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁
151	  isAffineOpen₀ := D.isAffineOpen₀.preimage (fst C (overSpec k R)).left
152	  isAffineOpen₁ := D.isAffineOpen₁.preimage (fst C (overSpec k R)).left
153	  sup_eq_top := by
154	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_sup, D.sup_eq_top, Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
155	  isAffineOpen_inf := by
156	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf]
157	    exact D.isAffineOpen_inf.preimage (fst C (overSpec k R)).left
158	
159	end PullbackProd

128	/-- **The dual-number test object** `Spec k[ε]` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`.
129	Its pointed `X`-valued points at a section `e` of a `k`-scheme `X` form the
130	Zariski tangent space `T_e X` (Mumford, "Abelian varieties", §II.4). -/
131	noncomputable def overDualNumber (k : Type u) [Field k] :
132	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
133	  Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k))))
134	
135	/-- **The `ε ↦ 0` point** `Spec k ⟶ Spec k[ε]`, as a morphism in
136	`Over (Spec k)` out of the trivial over-object. Restricting a tangent vector
137	along it recovers the underlying point. -/
138	noncomputable def overDualNumberZero (k : Type u) [Field k] :
139	    Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ⟶ overDualNumber k :=
140	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TruncExpCech.fstRingHom (R := k))))
141	    (specMap_fstRingHom_comp k)
142	
143	/-- **The augmentation** `Spec k[ε] ⟶ Spec k`, as a morphism in `Over (Spec k)`
144	into the trivial over-object. Composition with it produces the "constant"
145	tangent vectors. -/
146	noncomputable def overDualNumberAugment (k : Type u) [Field k] :
147	    overDualNumber k ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
148	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k))))
149	    (Category.comp_id _)
150	
151	/-- The `ε ↦ 0` point and the augmentation form a retract pair. -/
152	lemma overDualNumberZero_comp_augment (k : Type u) [Field k] :
153	    overDualNumberZero k ≫ overDualNumberAugment k
154	      = 𝟙 (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) := by
155	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
156	  exact specMap_fstRingHom_comp k
157	
158	/-! ## §3. Sections through a common point coincide -/
159	
160	/-- **Two sections of a `k`-scheme through the same point coincide.** For a
161	scheme `X` over `Spec k` and sections `e₁, e₂` of the structure morphism with
162	`e₁(*) = e₂(*)`, already `e₁ = e₂`: the common image point is `k`-rational
163	(`bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section`), a morphism `Spec k ⟶ X` at a
164	fixed point is determined by its stalk data (`specToEquivOfLocalRingAt`), and
165	the stalk data of a section is a *local retraction* `𝒪_{X,x} → k` of the
166	structure homomorphism — unique at a rational point
167	(`IsLocalRing.ringHom_ext_of_surjective_residue_comp`). -/
168	theorem overSection_ext (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
169	    {e₁ e₂ : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
170	    (h₁ : e₁ ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
171	    (h₂ : e₂ ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
172	    (hbase : e₁.base default = e₂.base default) :
173	    e₁ = e₂ := by
174	  haveI : IsLocalRing ↥(CommRingCat.of k) := inferInstanceAs (IsLocalRing k)
175	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
176	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
177	  set x : X.left := e₂.base (closedPoint ↥(CommRingCat.of k)) with hxdef
178	  have hb₂ : e₂.base (closedPoint ↥(CommRingCat.of k)) = x := hxdef.symm
179	  have hb₁ : e₁.base (closedPoint ↥(CommRingCat.of k)) = x :=
180	    (congrArg e₁.base (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).trans <|
181	      hbase.trans <| (congrArg e₂.base (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).trans hb₂
182	  have hres : Function.Surjective
183	      (algebraMap k (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x))) :=
184	    (bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X h₂
185	      ((congrArg e₂.base (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).trans hb₂)).2
186	  have hres' : Function.Surjective
187	      ((residue (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)).comp (stalkStructureHom X.hom x).hom) := by
188	    intro y
189	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hres y
190	    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
191	    have hra : residue (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
192	        (algebraMap k (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) c)
193	          = algebraMap k (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) c :=
194	      residue_algebraMap c
195	    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, ← algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra X x, hra, hc]
196	  let E := specToEquivOfLocalRingAt X.left (CommRingCat.of k) x
197	  have hE : E ⟨e₁, hb₁⟩ = E ⟨e₂, hb₂⟩ := by
198	    apply Subtype.ext
199	    have hv₁ : (E ⟨e₁, hb₁⟩).1
200	        = (X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hb₁.symm)).hom ≫
201	            Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e₁ := rfl
202	    have hv₂ : (E ⟨e₂, hb₂⟩).1
203	        = (X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hb₂.symm)).hom ≫
204	            Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e₂ := rfl
205	    rw [hv₁, hv₂]
206	    haveI : IsLocalHom ((X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr
207	        (Inseparable.of_eq hb₁.symm)).hom).hom := isLocalHom_of_isIso _
208	    haveI : IsLocalHom ((X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr
209	        (Inseparable.of_eq hb₂.symm)).hom).hom := isLocalHom_of_isIso _
210	    have hc₁ : stalkStructureHom X.hom x ≫
211	        (X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hb₁.symm)).hom ≫
212	          Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e₁ = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k) :=
213	      (comp_eq_spec_iff_of_base_eq X.hom hb₁ (𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k))).mp
214	        (by rw [Spec.map_id]; exact h₁)
215	    have hc₂ : stalkStructureHom X.hom x ≫
216	        (X.left.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hb₂.symm)).hom ≫
217	          Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e₂ = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k) :=
218	      (comp_eq_spec_iff_of_base_eq X.hom hb₂ (𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k))).mp
219	        (by rw [Spec.map_id]; exact h₂)

160	/-! ## The truncated exponential detects the additive coboundaries -/
161	
162	/-- **The truncated exponential detects the additive coboundaries** (the
163	well-definedness/injectivity heart of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle leg): the unit
164	`1 + b ε` on the dual-number overlap ring is a coboundary of the thickened cover iff
165	`b` is an additive coboundary `ρ₁(a₁) + ρ₂(a₂)`.
166	
167	Forward direction: decompose the two chart units `wᵢ ∈ (Aᵢ[ε])ˣ` as
168	`inl(wᵢ₀)·(1 + cᵢ ε)` (`unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit`); reducing the coboundary
169	relation mod `ε` forces the constant parts to cancel, leaving
170	`1 + b ε = 1 + (ρ₁ c₁ + ρ₂ c₂) ε`. -/
171	theorem truncExpUnit_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_iff
172	    (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) (b : B) :
173	    truncExpUnit b ∈ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
174	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ := by
175	  constructor
176	  · intro h
177	    obtain ⟨w₁, w₂, hw⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp h
178	    rw [← unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit w₁,
179	      ← unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit w₂, map_mul, map_mul,
180	      unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl, unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl,
181	      map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit,
182	      mul_mul_mul_comm, ← map_mul, ← truncExpUnit_add] at hw
183	    -- reduce mod `ε`: the constant part of the coboundary is trivial
184	    have hfst := congrArg unitsFst hw
185	    rw [map_mul, unitsFst_unitsInl, unitsFst_truncExpUnit, mul_one,
186	      unitsFst_truncExpUnit] at hfst
187	    rw [hfst, map_one, one_mul] at hw
188	    exact mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mpr ⟨_, _, truncExpUnit_injective hw⟩
189	  · intro h
190	    obtain ⟨a₁, a₂, rfl⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mp h
191	    refine mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr ⟨truncExpUnit a₁, truncExpUnit a₂, ?_⟩
192	    rw [map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, ← truncExpUnit_add]
193	
194	/-! ## The Čech reduction map and its kernel -/
195	
196	/-- Reduction mod `ε` on units carries thickened coboundaries to coboundaries
197	(`unitsFst` naturality), so it descends to the Čech `Ȟ¹` quotients. -/
198	theorem cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsFst (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
199	    cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂) ≤
200	      (cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂).comap (unitsFst (R := B)) := by
201	  intro u hu
202	  obtain ⟨w₁, w₂, rfl⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
203	  refine Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr
204	    ⟨unitsFst w₁, unitsFst w₂, ?_⟩)
205	  rw [map_mul, unitsFst_map_mapRingHom, unitsFst_map_mapRingHom]
206	
207	/-- **The reduction map of two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`-of-units groups**
208	`Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)` induced by reduction mod `ε` — the Čech-cocycle incarnation of
209	the restriction `Pic(C ×_k Spec k[ε]) → Pic(C)` along `ε ↦ 0`. Its kernel is computed
210	by `truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv` below. -/
211	noncomputable def cechUnitsReduction (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
212	    ((B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) →*
213	      Bˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂ :=
214	  QuotientGroup.map _ _ (unitsFst (R := B))
215	    (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsFst ρ₁ ρ₂)
216	
217	/-- Truncated-exponential classes lie in the kernel of the Čech reduction map:
218	`1 + b ε` reduces to `1` mod `ε`. -/
219	theorem cechUnitsReduction_mk_truncExpUnit (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
220	    (b : B) :
221	    cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂ (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b)) = 1 := by
222	  rw [cechUnitsReduction, QuotientGroup.map_mk, unitsFst_truncExpUnit,
223	    QuotientGroup.mk_one]
224	
225	/-- Vanishing of a truncated-exponential class in the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`:
226	`[1 + b ε] = 1` iff `b` is an additive coboundary. -/
227	theorem mk_truncExpUnit_eq_one_iff (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) (b : B) :
228	    (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
229	        (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) = 1
230	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ := by
231	  rw [QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
232	  exact truncExpUnit_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_iff ρ₁ ρ₂ b
233	
234	/-- **Every kernel class of the Čech reduction is a truncated exponential** (the
235	surjectivity heart of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle leg): a class of `Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε])`
236	restricting trivially mod `ε` is represented by `1 + b ε` for some `b : B`. Proof:
237	normalise a representative `u` by the (lifted) chart units trivialising its reduction;
238	the corrected unit has trivial constant part, hence lies in the range of the truncated
239	exponential (`truncExp_range_eq_ker_unitsFst`). -/
240	theorem exists_mk_truncExpUnit_of_cechUnitsReduction_eq_one
241	    (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
242	    (x : (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂))
243	    (hx : cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂ x = 1) :
244	    ∃ b : B, (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
245	      (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) = x := by
246	  revert hx
247	  induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
248	  | H u =>
249	    intro hu
250	    rw [cechUnitsReduction, QuotientGroup.map_mk, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] at hu
251	    obtain ⟨v₁, v₂, hv⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
252	    -- the chart-unit correction of `u`
253	    have hker : unitsFst
254	        ((Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₁).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₁))⁻¹ * u *
255	          (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₂).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₂))⁻¹) = 1 := by
256	      rw [map_mul, map_mul, map_inv, map_inv, unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl,
257	        unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl, unitsFst_unitsInl, unitsFst_unitsInl, ← hv]
258	      group
259	    have hmem : (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₁).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₁))⁻¹ * u *
260	        (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₂).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₂))⁻¹
261	          ∈ (truncExp (R := B)).range := by
262	      rw [truncExp_range_eq_ker_unitsFst]
263	      exact MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr hker
264	    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := MonoidHom.mem_range.mp hmem
265	    refine ⟨m.toAdd, ?_⟩
266	    rw [← truncExp_apply, hm, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_mul,
267	      QuotientGroup.mk_inv, QuotientGroup.mk_inv,
268	      (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr
269	        (unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
270	          (unitsInl v₁)),
271	      (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr
272	        (unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_right (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
273	          (unitsInl v₂))]
274	    simp
275	
276	/-! ## The kernel computation -/
277

279	reduction map (multiplicative source `Multiplicative B`). -/

1	---
2	name: lean-check
3	description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
4	---
5	
6	## Required proof loop
7	
8	Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
9	at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
10	`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
11	before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
12	search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.
13	
14	Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
15	check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
16	validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
17	unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
18	usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
19	the check.
20	
21	LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
22	module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
23	configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
24	the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
25	only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
26	specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.
27	
28	- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
29	  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
30	  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
31	- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
32	  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
33	  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
34	  project root.
35	- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
36	  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
37	- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
38	- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
39	  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
40	- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
41	  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.
42	
43	## Fast LSP proving loop
44	
45	The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
46	(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:
47	
48	- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
49	  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
50	- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
51	  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
52	- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
53	  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
54	  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
55	- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
56	  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
57	  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
58	  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.
59	
60	Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
61	skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
62	candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
63	kernel-check the module at the end.
64	
65	## Heavy builds — actually wait for them
66	
67	Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
68	deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
69	ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
70	or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
71	"Warnings are work").
72	
73	A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
74	most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
75	build to finish**:
76	
77	- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
78	  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
79	  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
80	  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
81	- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
82	  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
83	  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
84	  is *not* done.
85	- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
86	  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
87	  for final validation.
88	- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
89	  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
90	  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
91	  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
92	- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
93	  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
94	  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
95	  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.
96	
97	## When the LSP dies on big import files
98	
99	The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
100	imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
101	that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
102	run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
103	proof error:
104	
105	- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
106	  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
107	  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
108	- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
109	  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
110	  the specific module you are proving in instead.
111	- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
112	  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.
