1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPic
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.DualNumberTestObject
8	
9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard group at a one-point test object (W5-T4, §6.0)
11	
12	At a test object `T` whose underlying space is a **single point** — the dual numbers
13	`Spec k[ε]` and the monoidal unit `Spec k` are the two cases Wave 5 uses — the subgroup
14	`picFromBase C T` of classes pulled back from the base is **trivial**, so
15	
16	```
17	relPic C T  ≃*  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic
18	```
19	
20	and the coset calculus of the relative Picard group disappears from the ε-kernel
21	computation entirely.
22	
23	## Why this is cheap, and why it was not found earlier
24	
25	`picFromBase C T` is the *range* of `CechPic.map (snd C T).left`, i.e. of a group
26	homomorphism **out of** `T.left.CechPic`. A one-point space admits no cover with a
27	nontrivial overlap, so its Čech `H¹` of units vanishes — this is
28	`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` (`Picard/Pic.lean`), landed with the Picard
29	group itself. The range of a homomorphism out of a subsingleton group is trivial, and that
30	is the whole proof.
31	
32	The `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` risk register (R-T4-1) had listed this collapse as a
33	sub-cliff of brick T4-b, to be paid by proving that `Pic` of a finite product of Artin
34	local rings vanishes. That statement is true and is genuine commutative algebra; it is also
35	*not needed at a one-point test*, where the collapse is topological. The lesson recorded in
36	that worksheet's §6.0: search for the shape of the **object** (a one-point space), not for
37	the shape of the expected **argument** (Artin local rings). The general-coefficient form
38	does still need the algebra, and is out of scope here.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton` — the collapse.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton` — hence `relPicMk` is injective.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMulEquivCechPic` — the resulting isomorphism
45	  `relPic C T ≃* (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic`, with the computation rule
46	  `relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk`.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_overDualNumber_left`,
48	  `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase_overDualNumber_eq_bot` — the two Wave-5 instances.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMap` — the compatibility square: the
50	  equivalence intertwines `relPicMap` with `CechPic.map`. This is what makes the reduction
51	  usable rather than merely true, since Wave 5 computes the *kernel* of the `ε`-restriction,
52	  not just the groups at its two ends.
53	
54	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020).
55	-/
56	
57	set_option autoImplicit false
58	
59	universe u
60	
61	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
62	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
63	
64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
65	
66	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
67	
68	/-! ## The collapse at a one-point test object -/
69	
70	/-- **`picFromBase` is trivial at a one-point test object.** Classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back
71	from `T` form the range of `CechPic.map (snd C T).left`; when `T.left` has a subsingleton
72	underlying space its Čech Picard group is trivial
73	(`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`), so that range is `⊥`.
74	
75	No hypothesis on `C` whatsoever, and no commutative algebra: the argument is that a
76	one-point space has no cover with a nontrivial overlap. -/
77	theorem picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
78	    [Subsingleton T.left] : picFromBase C T = ⊥ := by
79	  refine le_antisymm (fun L hL => ?_) bot_le
80	  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff (C := C)).mp hL
81	  rw [← hN, Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton _ N, map_one]
82	  exact Subgroup.mem_bot.mpr rfl
83	
84	/-- **The projection to the relative Picard group is injective at a one-point test
85	object** — immediate from `picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton`, since a quotient by the
86	trivial subgroup separates points. Together with the landed `relPicMk_surjective` this makes
87	`relPicMk` bijective. -/
88	theorem relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    [Subsingleton T.left] : Function.Injective (relPicMk C T) := by
90	  intro x y hxy
91	  have h := (QuotientGroup.eq (s := picFromBase C T)).mp hxy
92	  rw [picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton C T, Subgroup.mem_bot, inv_mul_eq_one] at h
93	  exact h
94	
95	/-- **`relPic C T ≃* Pic(C ⊗ T)` at a one-point test object.** The relative Picard group is
96	the *absolute* Čech Picard group of `C ⊗ T` there, because the subgroup being quotiented out
97	is trivial. This is what lets the Wave-5 ε-kernel computation be phrased on `CechPic`
98	directly, with no coset bookkeeping. -/
99	noncomputable def relPicMulEquivCechPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [Subsingleton T.left] :
100	    relPic C T ≃* (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic :=
101	  (MulEquiv.ofBijective (relPicMk C T)
102	    ⟨relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C T, relPicMk_surjective C T⟩).symm
103	
104	@[simp]
105	theorem relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [Subsingleton T.left]
106	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
107	    relPicMulEquivCechPic C T (relPicMk C T L) = L :=
108	  (MulEquiv.ofBijective (relPicMk C T)
109	    ⟨relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C T, relPicMk_surjective C T⟩).symm_apply_apply L
110	
111	/-! ## The two Wave-5 instances: `Spec k[ε]` and `Spec k` -/
112	
113	/-- The dual-number test object has a one-point underlying space: `Spec` of a local ring
114	whose maximal ideal is nilpotent. -/
115	instance subsingleton_overDualNumber_left :
116	    Subsingleton (overDualNumber k).left :=
117	  inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum (DualNumber k)))
118	
119	/-- **`picFromBase` is trivial at the dual-number test** — the Wave-5 instance of
120	`picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton`, retiring the "picFromBase collapse" sub-cliff that
121	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §4 (R-T4-1) had priced as commutative algebra. -/
122	theorem picFromBase_overDualNumber_eq_bot :
123	    picFromBase C (overDualNumber k) = ⊥ :=
124	  picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton C _
125	
126	/-- `relPic C (Spec k[ε]) ≃* Pic(C_ε)`: the ε-side of the Wave-5 kernel, with the relative
127	quotient removed. -/
128	noncomputable def relPicOverDualNumberMulEquivCechPic :
129	    relPic C (overDualNumber k) ≃* (C ⊗ overDualNumber k).left.CechPic :=
130	  relPicMulEquivCechPic C _
131	
132	/-! ## The compatibility square (what makes the reduction usable, not merely true) -/
133	
134	/-- **The equivalence intertwines restriction along `g` with pullback of Čech classes.**
135	
136	Without this, `relPicMulEquivCechPic` would identify the two *groups* at each end of the
137	`ε`-restriction while saying nothing about the *map* between them — and it is the kernel of
138	that map that Wave 5 computes. With it, the statement
139	`ker(relPic(k[ε]) → relPic(k)) ≃ ker(CechPic(C_ε) → CechPic(C))` is immediate.
140	
141	The proof is `relPicMap_mk`: the relative restriction is *defined* as `CechPic.map (C ◁ g)`
142	descended to the quotients, so once the quotient is trivial there is nothing left to check.
143	Recorded explicitly because "the groups agree" and "the maps agree" are different claims and
144	only the second one is usable. -/
145	theorem relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMap (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k)))
146	    [Subsingleton T.left] [Subsingleton T'.left] (g : T' ⟶ T) (x : relPic C T) :
147	    relPicMulEquivCechPic C T' (relPicMap C g x)
148	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (relPicMulEquivCechPic C T x) := by
149	  induction x using relPic.ind with
150	  | mk L => rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk, relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk]
151	
152	end AlgebraicGeometry
153
